sections.content: How many people are "market and street traders and assistants"?

8,060 people

were counted on the census as "market and street traders and assistants" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Market and street traders and assistants sell goods (other than refreshments) from stalls, barrows and other portable containers in streets and market places.

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "market and street traders and assistants" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 55 to 59 years. Of the whole working population 10.4% were aged 55 to 59 years. For people working as "market and street traders and assistants", 16.2% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "market and street traders and assistants" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "market and street traders and assistants" included:

  • launderers, dry cleaners and pressers
  • roundspersons and van salespersons
  • upholsterers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "market and street traders and assistants" there were more men than women (66.1% compared with 33.9%).

This means "market and street traders and assistants" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "sales occupations".

Men made up 66.1% and women made up 33.9% of "market and street traders and assistants"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "market and street traders and assistants" included:

  • managers and directors in the creative industries
  • police officers (sergeant and below)
  • IT project managers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "market and street traders and assistants" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "market and street traders and assistants" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "market and street traders and assistants", 15.1% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work part-time than full-time (52.2% compared with 47.8%).

They are also more likely to be self-employed (71.2%) than an employee (28.8%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
